AI.motivation: Overcome limitations of vision-only VAD (sensitivity to illumination, motion blur, and complex backgrounds) by leveraging event cameras' robustness to lighting and high temporal precision, and by integrating multi-modal signals (events, video, text).
AI.method: 1) Construct a large-scale visible-event benchmark (6.3B events, 376,368 frames). 2) Propose a contrastive multi-modal pretraining strategy aligning semantic embeddings across event streams, videos, and textual descriptions. 3) Develop an adaptive fusion module to dynamically fuse event-based temporal cues with video-based spatial semantics for robust VAD.
AI.result: EVAD achieves consistent improvements over baselines on standard benchmarks and the TJU TCM Pha dataset, demonstrating the effectiveness of event-based sensing for VAD in real-world scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Event-camera data, when coupled with contrastive multi-modal pretraining and adaptive fusion, offers robust and scalable improvements for video anomaly detection in challenging conditions.

title: Optimal Top-$k$ Identification from Pairwise Comparisons
summary: We study the active learning problem of fixed-confidence top-$k$ identification from noisy pairwise comparisons. In this problem, an algorithm sequentially chooses pairs of items to compare, observes the outcomes, and stops when it can return the set of top-$k$ items with error probability at most $δ$. The objective is to design such a $δ$-correct procedure that minimizes the expected number of comparisons (the sample complexity). This problem falls within the broader literature on fixed-confidence pure exploration in bandit models, where a common target is asymptotic optimality: the algorithm's expected sample complexity matches the information theoretic lower bound as $δ\to 0$. Asymptotically optimal procedures have been developed for a range of fixed-confidence pure-exploration problems, however to the best of our knowledge, for top-$1$, or more generally top-$k$ identification from pairwise comparisons under latent utility models an asymptotically optimal algorithm has not been established. In this setting, we develop such an algorithm. We characterize the structure of the lower bound and formulate it as a saddle-point problem. This structure enables a computationally efficient primal-dual procedure that learns the asymptotically optimal comparison allocation online. We then construct an adaptive comparison-allocation algorithm that tracks the allocation learned by the primal-dual procedure and prove it is asymptotically optimal.

AI.tldr: First asymptotically optimal fixed-confidence algorithm for top-k identification from noisy pairwise comparisons under latent utilities. It uses a saddle-point lower bound and a primal-dual online allocation to learn the optimal comparison strategy, with an adaptive algorithm that tracks this allocation and achieves asymptotic optimality.
AI.motivation: Addresses a gap in fixed-confidence pure-exploration for top-k identification in pairwise comparison models with latent utilities. Aims to minimize sample complexity (comparisons) as the error tolerance δ→0.
AI.method: Derives an information-theoretic lower bound and casts it as a saddle-point problem. Develops a computationally efficient primal-dual procedure to learn the asymptotically optimal comparison allocation online. Proposes an adaptive allocation algorithm that follows the learnt allocation and proves asymptotic optimality (matching the lower bound as δ→0).
AI.result: Characterizes the lower bound structure as a saddle-point; provides a practical primal-dual method to compute allocation; constructs an adaptive allocation algorithm that tracks this allocation during sampling; proves the algorithm is asymptotically optimal.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first asymptotically optimal algorithm for fixed-confidence top-k identification from noisy pairwise comparisons under latent models, advancing theory of pure-exploration in bandits and offering a concrete, scalable allocation scheme.

title: ConceptSMILE: Auditing the Trustworthiness of Concept-Based Explainable AI
summary: Concept-based explainable artificial intelligence (AI) can make model reasoning more human-understandable, but concept-level outputs are not automatically trustworthy. We introduce ConceptSMILE, a model-agnostic perturbation-based auditing framework for evaluating the reliability of concept-based explanations. Rather than replacing SMILE, ConceptSMILE extends its perturbation-based logic from feature- or region-level attribution to the auditing of human-understandable concept explanations. The framework perturbs input regions, measures concept-response shifts, applies locality weighting, and fits an XGBoost surrogate to approximate local concept behaviour. Reliability is assessed through attribution accuracy, surrogate fidelity, faithfulness, stability, and consistency. We evaluate ConceptSMILE on retinal fundus images by comparing MedSAM-derived visual concepts with VLM-based semantic concepts. Results show that reliability varies across concepts and pathways: MedSAM achieves stronger spatial attribution and the highest surrogate fidelity ($R^2 = 0.8503$, $R_w^2 = 0.8465$), while the VLM pathway shows stronger vessel faithfulness and stronger stability under selected artefact conditions. ConceptSMILE provides an independent audit layer for evaluating the trustworthiness of concept-based XAI.

AI.tldr: ConceptSMILE is a model-agnostic, perturbation-based auditing framework to evaluate the trustworthiness of concept-based explanations, extending SMILE to concept-level outputs; it perturbs input regions, uses locality weighting, and fits an XGBoost surrogate to assess reliability across attribution accuracy, fidelity, faithfulness, stability, and consistency, with retinal fundus experiments showing variable reliability across concepts and pathways (MedSAM yields high surrogate fidelity; VLM yields strong vessel faithfulness and stability).
AI.motivation: Concept-based explanations for AI can be human-understandable but lack automatic trust guarantees. There is a need for an independent auditing layer to assess the reliability of concept-level explanations.
AI.method: Perturb input regions to elicit concept-response shifts, apply locality weighting, fit an XGBoost surrogate to approximate local concept behavior, and evaluate reliability via attribution accuracy, surrogate fidelity (R^2), faithfulness, stability, and consistency. Compare MedSAM-derived visual concepts with VLM-based semantic concepts on retinal fundus images.
AI.result: MedSAM shows stronger spatial attribution and highest surrogate fidelity (R^2 = 0.8503, R_w^2 = 0.8465); the VLM pathway demonstrates stronger vessel faithfulness and greater stability under selected artefact conditions. Reliability of concept explanations varies across concepts and pathways.
AI.conclusion: ConceptSMILE provides an independent auditing layer to evaluate the trustworthiness of concept-based XAI, highlighting that reliability is context- and pathway-dependent and that multiple pathways may be needed for robust auditing.

title: Event Burst Trigger: An Availability Backdoor Attack on Event-Based SNN Object Detection
comment: The 56th Annual IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Dependable Systems and Networks (DSN 2026)
summary: Event-based vision and spiking neural networks (SNNs) are increasingly adopted for edge intelligence under strict latency and energy constraints. However, the vulnerability of event-based SNN object detection models to availability backdoor attacks remains insufficiently studied. This paper presents Event Burst Trigger (EBT), an availability backdoor attack targeting SNN-based object detection models. EBT injects carefully crafted event-based triggers into the training data, which induce temporally concentrated event streams during inference. These burst-like activations increase the number of phantom (i.e., spurious) object candidates, and consequently inflate the computational cost of the post-processing stage, particularly Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS). We evaluate EBT on SpikeYOLO, the state-of-the-art SNN-based object detector, under a poison-only threat model that does not require modifications to the model architecture, loss function, or inference pipeline. Experimental results show that while detection accuracy remains largely preserved, with mAP@0.5 decreasing by less than 0.099, the latency of the NMS stage increases by up to 38%. This indicates that NMS can become a dominant availability bottleneck in event-based SNN object detection. Experiments on an edge platform further show that the proposed attack elevates baseline resource utilization and reduces scheduling slack without inducing conspicuous peaks in resource usage. In addition, STRIP-based backdoor detection fails to reliably distinguish the proposed attack from benign inputs. These results characterize a previously underexplored availability backdoor threat in event-based SNN object detection systems.

AI.tldr: An availability backdoor named Event Burst Trigger (EBT) targets SNN-based object detectors by inserting event-based triggers that induce bursts of temporally concentrated events, inflating Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) latency while largely preserving detection accuracy.
AI.motivation: Edge intelligence with event-based SNNs faces strict latency/energy constraints; NMS can become a bottleneck and availability attacks on such systems are underexplored.
AI.method: Inject carefully crafted event-based triggers during training (poison-only threat model) to cause burst-like activations at inference, increasing phantom object candidates and NMS workload without altering model architecture, loss, or inference pipeline; evaluate on SpikeYOLO and on edge platform; use STRIP for defense analysis.
AI.result: mAP@0.5 degrades by <0.099 (nearly preserved accuracy); NMS latency increases by up to 38%; higher resource utilization and reduced scheduling slack observed; STRIP-based backdoor detection fails to reliably distinguish attack from benign inputs.
AI.conclusion: EBT reveals a previously underexplored availability backdoor threat in event-based SNN object detection where NMS becomes the bottleneck; defenses must consider post-processing-stage vulnerabilities and more robust backdoor detectors.

title: AlphaZero in Sparsely Rewarded Games: Limits and Auxiliary Supervision
summary: AlphaZero has demonstrated that a neural-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search can achieve superhuman performance, but strong play does not necessarily imply perfect play. We study this gap in two oracle-evaluable domains with contrasting structure: Connect Four, a solved partisan game with exact game-theoretic values, and Chomp, an impartial game whose optimal play is governed by Grundy-number structure. Under a unified self-play $+$ MCTS pipeline, we compare vanilla AlphaZero, a multi-frame variant (limited to Chomp), and an AlphaZero Auxiliary Loss (AZAL) that adds oracle-derived policy supervision. We find that vanilla AlphaZero achieves strong play across both domains but cannot preserve the exact trajectories required for optimal play: in Connect Four, it fails to maintain the optimal line of play, while in Chomp, it fails to consistently restore the $g=0$ invariant. On rectangular Chomp boards, multi-frame inputs alone do not remove this gap. Nevertheless, AZAL substantially improves oracle consistency across multi-seeded full-game traces and sampled-state evaluations. On Chomp, AZAL reaches perfect full-game oracle consistency on 10x11 and high but not complete consistency on 9x10; on Connect Four, AZAL improves oracle-match rate and delays the first oracle mistake, but does not reach perfect play.

AI.tldr: AZAL (oracle-guided policy supervision) improves trajectory alignment with perfect play in neural-guided MCTS; vanilla AlphaZero achieves strong play but not exact-optimal trajectories in Connect Four (line of play) and Chomp (g=0 invariant). Multi-frame inputs help little; AZAL yields perfect full-game oracle consistency on 10x11 Chomp and high-but-not-complete on 9x10, with notable improvements in Connect Four but not perfect.
AI.motivation: Investigate the gap between strong play and perfect play in neural-guided MCTS agents, across domains with different combinatorial structure (solved partisan vs impartial with Grundy numbers), and assess whether oracle-derived supervision can enforce optimal trajectories without sacrificing performance.
AI.method: Unified self-play + MCTS pipeline evaluating three agents: vanilla AlphaZero, a multi-frame Chomp variant, and AZAL (AlphaZero Auxiliary Loss with oracle-derived policy supervision). Domains: Connect Four and Chomp (rectangular boards). Metrics include oracle consistency, Grundy-trajectory invariants (g=0), oracle-match rate, and timing of oracle mistakes across full-game traces and sampled states.
AI.result: Vanilla AlphaZero delivers strong play in both domains but fails to preserve exact optimal trajectories: Connect Four lacks the optimal line of play; Chomp fails to restore the g=0 invariant. On rectangular Chomp boards, multi-frame inputs do not close the gap. AZAL substantially improves trajectory/oracle consistency, achieving perfect full-game oracle consistency on 10x11 Chomp and high-but-not-complete consistency on 9x10; in Connect Four, AZAL improves oracle-match rate and delays the first oracle mistake but does not attain perfect play.
AI.conclusion: Oracle-guided supervision (AZAL) substantially improves alignment with exact, oracle-defined play in neural-guided MCTS, especially for impartial games with Grundy structure (Chomp). However, even with AZAL, perfect play is not universally achieved (notably in Connect Four), indicating limits to trajectory fidelity under neural-guided MCTS and the need for domain-aware supervision strategies or stronger priors.

title: Causally Debiased Latent Action Model for Embodied Action Conditioned World Models
summary: Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) aim to simulate future observations conditioned on embodied actions, offering a promising foundation for robot planning, policy evaluation, and data augmentation. However, learning controllable ACWMs requires large-scale action-labeled data, which remains costly to collect in the real world. Latent action models (LAMs) mitigate this bottleneck by inferring latent actions from unlabeled videos, but existing LAMs are typically trained with reconstruction-only objectives and therefore entangle action-relevant dynamics with action-irrelevant visual factors such as backgrounds and untouched objects. In this work, we identify this action-irrelevant bias as a key obstacle to controllable ACWMs and introduce evaluation metrics to measure latent-action bias, action following, and robustness. We propose CD-LAM, a causally debiased framework for LAM-based ACWMs. CD-LAM introduces three efficient fine-tuning objectives: embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, and latent space calibration, which together encourage embodiment-focused, action-aware, and calibrated non-collapsed latent action representations. Experiments on 2B and 14B ACWM backbones show that CD-LAM substantially improves latent-action controllability, downstream robot-action following, visual fidelity, and adaptation efficiency, requiring only 6k fine-tuning steps and more than 12$\times$ fewer robot-action adaptation updates than the baseline.

AI.tldr: CD-LAM: a causally debiased latent-action model for action-conditioned world models that uses three fine-tuning objectives—embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, and latent-space calibration—to produce embodied, action-aware, calibrated latent actions, improving controllability and adaptation with minimal fine-tuning on large ACWM backbones.
AI.motivation: Latent-action models trained with reconstruction objectives entangle action-relevant dynamics with action-irrelevant visual factors, hindering controllability and data efficiency; need metrics to measure latent-action bias and robust, controllable ACWMs; propose a debiased approach to leverage unlabeled data for ACWMs.
AI.method: CD-LAM framework with three objectives: embodiment-centric reconstruction, action-centric contrastive learning, latent-space calibration; efficient fine-tuning; evaluation on 2B and 14B backbones; introduces metrics for latent-action bias, action following, robustness.
AI.result: Substantial improvements in latent-action controllability, robot-action following, visual fidelity, and adaptation efficiency; only 6k fine-tuning steps; >12x fewer robot-action adaptation updates than baseline.
AI.conclusion: CD-LAM demonstrates effective debiasing of latent actions in LAM-based ACWMs, enabling controllable, data-efficient adaptation for large-scale action-conditioned world models.

title: 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction from Low-Overlap Captures
comment: Accepted to SIGGRAPH Conference Papers '26. First two authors contributed equally. Project page: https://sisyphm.github.io/studiorecon-page/
summary: Existing volumetric capture of dynamic human performance achieves high fidelity with dense camera arrays. However, in real-world scenarios, only a handful of low-overlap cameras are available, which degrades the output quality and leaves large areas unobserved. Recent 4D reconstruction methods have focused on low-overlap settings, yet they still produce noticeable artifacts in under-observed regions. Video diffusion models have emerged as another option, but they show geometrically inconsistent results for humans. To address these limitations, we propose StudioRecon, a pipeline that reconstructs 4D human scenes from sparse, low-overlap cameras by decoupling background and humans. We densify background supervision by synthesizing hundreds of camera-controlled novel views with a video diffusion model. We also robustly initialize deformable Gaussian humans with cross-view identity association and triangulated multi-view keypoint fitting. Finally, our recursive enhancement module with motion-adaptive consistency injection harmonizes the composed output, thereby further avoiding remaining artifacts. We achieve state-of-the-art novel view synthesis across four real-world datasets and demonstrate applications such as novel trajectory rendering and human replacement.

AI.tldr: StudioRecon enables 4D human reconstruction from sparse, low-overlap cameras by decoupling backgrounds from humans, densifying background with diffusion-generated novel views, robustizing human initialization via cross-view identity association and triangulated keypoints, and refining output with a motion-aware recursive enhancer.
AI.motivation: Real-world volumetric capture is often constrained to sparse camera setups with low overlap, leading to poor coverage and artifacts in unobserved regions. Existing 4D reconstruction and video diffusion approaches struggle under these conditions; a method that robustly reconstructs dynamic humans from sparse views is needed.
AI.method: Decouple background and foreground; densify background supervision via video diffusion-based synthesis of hundreds of novel views; initialize deformable Gaussian humans using cross-view identity association and triangulated multi-view keypoints; apply a recursive enhancement module with motion-adaptive consistency injection to harmonize outputs and reduce artifacts.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art novel view synthesis on four real-world datasets; demonstrates applications including novel trajectory rendering and human replacement.
AI.conclusion: StudioRecon offers a practical pipeline for high-quality 4D human reconstruction in sparse-view scenarios by combining diffusion-based background synthesis, robust multi-view human initialization, and a dynamic-consistency enhancement stage; it advances robustness and visual fidelity in under-observed regions.

title: Group Invariant Spectral Embedding
summary: Spectral embedding methods are widely used for dimensionality reduction and clustering of high-dimensional datasets with intrinsic low-dimensional structures. Although many datasets of practical interest exhibit invariance under symmetries such as rotations, standard spectral embedding methods do not account for this, treating symmetry-related data points as unrelated. Our approach to this problem is to incorporate the symmetries directly into the affinity kernels used for spectral embedding. We analyze the case of a Riemannian data manifold $M$ with symmetries given by a compact Lie group~$G$ and prove that, under suitable conditions, graph Laplacians constructed from three types of invariant kernels converge pointwise to explicit second-order differential operators on the quotient space $M/G$. Our analysis implies improved convergence rates, as the effective dimension drops according to the dimension of the group. We validate our approach on datasets with $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ or $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry, and show that $G$-invariant spectral embedding recovers the intrinsic geometry of the data, in contrast to standard spectral embedding, which fails to do so even in the limit of infinite data.

AI.tldr: Invariant kernels under compact Lie group symmetries yield graph Laplacians that converge to diffusion operators on the quotient M/G, improving convergence by reducing effective dimension; validated on SO(2) and SO(3).
AI.motivation: Datasets often exhibit symmetries (e.g., rotations); standard spectral embeddings ignore these, misrepresent geometry and slow convergence; incorporating symmetry into kernels aligns embeddings with intrinsic structure.
AI.method: Assume a Riemannian manifold M with symmetry group G; construct three invariant kernels; build graph Laplacians; prove pointwise convergence to explicit second-order differential operators on M/G; show convergence rate improvements due to dimension drop; empirical validation on datasets with SO(2)/SO(3) symmetry.
AI.result: Proved convergence of invariant- kernel graph Laplacians to differential operators on M/G; observed faster convergence due to effective dimension drop equal to dim G; G-invariant spectral embedding recovers intrinsic geometry, unlike standard embedding.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating symmetries into spectral methods yields faithful geometric recovery and improved asymptotics; approach generalizable to other compact Lie groups; has practical impact for data with rotational invariances.

title: Shortcut Trajectory Planning for Efficient Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Diffusion-based trajectory planners have shown strong performance in offline reinforcement learning, but their iterative denoising process often incurs high inference cost. Consistency-based planners reduce the number of sampling steps, yet they typically rely on a two-stage teacher--student distillation pipeline that increases training cost and may introduce instability. We propose Shortcut Trajectory Planning (STP), an offline model-based reinforcement learning framework that incorporates shortcut models as efficient trajectory generators. STP trains a conditional shortcut trajectory model in a single stage, supports adjustable one-step and few-step inference through step-size conditioning, and selects candidate plans using a critic augmented with feasibility-aware correction. Across standard D4RL benchmarks, including locomotion, navigation, manipulation, and dexterous control tasks, STP achieves strong performance while simplifying the training pipeline for fast generative planning.

AI.tldr: STP introduces a single-stage conditional shortcut trajectory model with step-size conditioning and a feasibility-aware critic for fast one-/few-step offline model-based planning, outperforming diffusion-based planners while simplifying training.
AI.motivation: Diffusion-based trajectory planners are accurate but expensive due to iterative denoising; consistency-based methods reduce sampling steps but rely on costly two-stage distillation and can be unstable.
AI.method: Train a conditional shortcut trajectory model in one stage for offline model-based RL. Use step-size conditioning to enable adjustable one-/few-step inference. Employ a feasibility-aware critic to select candidate plans and correct infeasibility.
AI.result: STP achieves strong performance on standard D4RL tasks (locomotion, navigation, manipulation, dexterous control) with faster planning and a simplified training pipeline compared to diffusion-based or distillation-based approaches.
AI.conclusion: STP offers an efficient, adaptable trajectory planning framework that reduces training complexity and inference cost while maintaining strong performance across diverse offline tasks; it broadens the practicality of model-based planning in offline RL.

title: VTaMo: Video-Text Alignment Model for Sign Language Translation
comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables. Accepted to ECCV 2026
summary: Sign language translation (SLT) converts continuous sign videos into spoken language text. Gloss-free approaches leverage pre-trained visual encoders and language models but rely on implicit cross-modal alignment from translation supervision alone. We present VTaMo, a framework that introduces explicit multi-granularity alignment at three levels: (1) local alignment via entropy-regularized optimal transport with a learnable null token for fine-grained frame-to-token correspondences; (2) global alignment via a learnable orthogonal transformation that calibrates embedding space geometry through Earth Mover's Distance; and (3) position-aligned contrastive learning for discriminative token-level representations. Experiments on Phoenix-2014T, CSL-Daily, How2Sign, and OpenASL demonstrate consistent state-of-the-art performance, with ablations confirming the complementary contributions of each component. Code is available at https://github.com/junyi2005/vtamo.

AI.tldr: VTaMo introduces explicit multi-granularity alignment for gloss-free SLT via three components: local OT-based frame-to-token alignment with a learnable null token, global space calibration through a learnable orthogonal transform, and position-aware contrastive learning to yield discriminative token representations; achieves state-of-the-art on multiple SLT benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Address the limited cross-modal alignment in gloss-free SLT relying solely on translation supervision; improve frame-to-token alignment, embedding space geometry, and token-level discriminability.
AI.method: Three-level alignment: (1) local alignment using entropy-regularized optimal transport with a learnable null token to obtain fine-grained frame-to-token correspondences; (2) global alignment with a learnable orthogonal transformation to calibrate embedding-space geometry via Earth Mover's Distance; (3) position-aligned contrastive learning for discriminative token-level representations.
AI.result: Consistent state-of-the-art across Phoenix-2014T, CSL-Daily, How2Sign, and OpenASL; ablation studies show each component contributes complementary gains.
AI.conclusion: Explicit multi-granularity alignment significantly improves gloss-free SLT performance; the three components are complementary, and the approach is reproducible with released code.

title: Sensitivity-Aware Thresholding and Token Routing for Activation Sparsification in Large Language Models
summary: Efficient inference in Large Language Models (LLMs) requires deciding where computation can be reduced while preserving model quality. We study this problem through multilayer perceptron (MLP) activation sparsification and token-level conditional routing. We first propose Sensitivity-Aware Thresholding for Sparsity (SATS), a threshold calibration method to choose layerwise gate thresholds using a local MLP output sensitivity proxy rather than calibrating thresholds directly from activation percentiles. While SATS retains the existing mechanism of sparsifying MLP activations by thresholding gate activations, it replaces percentile-based calibration with a sensitivity-aware selection rule. We then introduce a lightweight token routing framework that dynamically selects between a base path and a modified path on a per-token basis, rather than applying the modified computation uniformly to all tokens. We evaluate both methods on multiple recent open-weight LLMs. Our results show that SATS improves over the threshold-based sparsification baseline at matched actual sparsity and that token routing yields a more favorable quality-throughput trade-off than static activation modification baselines. Overall, our results suggest that improved threshold calibration and token routing can improve the quality-throughput trade-off in LLMs.

AI.tldr: Proposes SATS for MLP activation sparsification using a sensitivity proxy for threshold calibration, and a per-token dynamic routing framework; both improve quality-throughput trade-offs in open-weight LLMs compared to baseline approaches.
AI.motivation: Efficient LLM inference requires reducing computation without sacrificing model quality. Activation-sparsification through percentile-based thresholds may misalign with actual sensitivity. token-level routing can exploit per-token variability to improve efficiency.
AI.method: 1) SATS calibrates layerwise gate thresholds via a local MLP output sensitivity proxy rather than activation-percentile calibration. 2) A lightweight per-token routing framework chooses between a base path and a modified path for each token instead of applying the modified computation uniformly.
AI.result: SATS outperforms threshold-based sparsification at matched sparsity. Token routing yields a more favorable quality-throughput trade-off than static activation-modification baselines across multiple open-weight LLMs.
AI.conclusion: Improved threshold calibration and per-token routing can enhance the quality-throughput trade-off in LLMs, suggesting practical gains for efficient inference.

title: Hydra++: Real-Time Hierarchical 3D Scene Graph Construction With Object-Level Shape Estimation
comment: 8 pages, 12 figures, accepted in Proc. IEEE/RSJ IROS
summary: 3D scene graphs provide a hierarchical abstraction of environments by encoding spatial entities, such as objects and places, and their relationships. However, existing scene graph systems model object geometry coarsely, relying on partial point clouds or class-level CAD templates, which limits instance-specific shape detail. This paper presents Hydra++, a system-level investigation into how learning-based object shape estimators can be integrated into a hierarchical 3D scene graph pipeline. Hydra++ incorporates category-agnostic shape estimation and a reprojection-mask consistency check to reject degenerate predictions from partial observations or imprecise segmentation. In its default CRISP-based configuration, Hydra++ performs online scene graph construction; slower estimators such as SAM3D are evaluated as modular alternatives to demonstrate generalization-latency trade-offs. Furthermore, to address the challenges of sparse and noisy depth measurements in outdoor environments, Hydra++ supports a hybrid LiDAR-camera configuration for large-scale operation, improving scene-level reconstruction quality. Experiments in both simulation and real-world outdoor campus scenarios demonstrate that Hydra++ improves object- and scene-level reconstruction quality. Project page is available at https://hydra-plusplus.github.io/.

AI.tldr: Hydra++ enhances hierarchical 3D scene graphs by integrating category-agnostic learned shape estimators with a reprojection-mask consistency check, enabling online scene graph construction, modular estimator options (e.g., SAM3D), and a hybrid LiDAR-camera setup for outdoor scalability, leading to improved object- and scene-level reconstruction in both simulated and real-world campus environments.
AI.motivation: Existing scene-graph pipelines rely on coarse object geometry from partial point clouds or class-level CAD templates, which limits instance-specific shape fidelity and robust performance in streaming and outdoor settings. There is a need for integrating learned shape priors into a scalable, online scene-graph framework that can handle noisy depth data and varying sensor configurations.
AI.method: Integrate category-agnostic shape estimation into a hierarchical 3D scene-graph pipeline; apply a reprojection-mask consistency check to filter degenerate or unreliable predictions; default to CRISP-based online scene graph construction; evaluate slower estimators (e.g., SAM3D) as modular alternatives to study generalization-latency trade-offs; adopt a hybrid LiDAR-camera configuration to improve outdoor, large-scale scene reconstruction; validate on simulation and real-world outdoor campus scenarios.
AI.result: Hydra++ achieves improved object- and scene-level reconstruction quality in both simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating effective integration of learned shape estimators, robustness to partial observations, and scalability to outdoor environments.
AI.conclusion: Hydra++ represents a flexible, system-level framework for incorporating learning-based shape estimators into online hierarchical 3D scene graphs, balancing accuracy and latency, and enabling outdoor deployment via sensor fusion. It provides a testbed for comparing estimators and settings (e.g., CRISP online configuration versus modular backends like SAM3D) and establishes practical benefits for large-scale reconstruction.

title: IB-Flow: Information Bottleneck-Guided CFG Distillation for Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
summary: While large-scale text-to-image generative models have achieved unprecedented visual performance, their inherent reliance on multi-step iterative solvers incurs severe inference latency. Few-step distillation targeting the Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) trajectory has emerged as the prevalent dual-dimensional compression paradigm. However, existing frameworks remain subjugated by a coarse-grained blind injection paradigm that perpetually enforces a globally static guidance strength while indiscriminately sampling the supervisor timestep. This state-agnostic design completely disregards the intrinsic nature of image generation as a dynamic evolutionary process characterized by progressive entropy reduction, which not only restricts the performance boundary of few-step compression but also precipitates severe CFG over-conditioning artifacts. To transcend these limitations, we re-examine the distillation procedure through the theoretical lens of Information Theory, formally modeling it as a dynamic mutual information game constrained by the Information Bottleneck (IB) principle. Specifically, we dismantle traditional blind assumptions via a dual-track adaptive framework. To determine the injection target, we propose an instance-aware selection mechanism that transmutes the intractable KL divergence constraint into a zero-overhead closed-form solution predicated on the local vector field norm. To regulate the injection strength, we introduce an entropy-aware schedule that dynamically decays alongside the SNR, applying maximal thrust for initial structural anchoring before smoothly reverting to the natural manifold to refine micro-details. Extensive empirical evaluations corroborate that our framework fundamentally eradicates over-conditioning artifacts, shattering the performance ceiling to achieve SOTA generative fidelity under extremely stringent 2-step configurations.

AI.tldr: An information-theoretic dynamic distillation for few-step CFG in text-to-image diffusion; uses instance-aware injection target and entropy-aware schedule to avoid over-conditioning, achieving state-of-the-art fidelity with only 2 steps.
AI.motivation: Mitigate latency from multi-step diffusion by replacing coarse, static guidance with a dynamic, information-theoretic framework. Current CFG distillation imposes a static guidance strength and blind supervisor-timestep selection, causing suboptimal fidelity and over-conditioning. Treat image synthesis as a dynamic entropy-reducing process and apply the Information Bottleneck to optimize guidance.
AI.method: Formulate the distillation as a dynamic mutual-information game under the Information Bottleneck principle. Replace KL constraint with a zero-overhead closed-form based on local vector-field norm for injection target; introduce an instance-aware target selection; implement an entropy-aware schedule that decays with SNR, providing strong early guidance and gradual refinement; operate within a dual-track adaptive framework that adaptively governs injection and guidance.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show removal of over-conditioning artifacts and a new performance ceiling for 2-step CFG distillation, achieving state-of-the-art generative fidelity under extremely stringent 2-step configurations.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic, IB-guided distillation with instance-aware injection and entropy-aware scheduling substantially improves few-step diffusion performance, eliminating over-conditioning and pushing the limits of 2-step CFG-based generation.

title: Model Agnostic Graph Prompt Learning for Crystal Property Prediction
summary: Graph Neural Networks have emerged as a powerful tool for the fast and accurate prediction of various crystal properties. These models often encode domain-specific knowledge into their graph encoding modules, which increases their parameter size and makes their performance heavily dependent on domain expertise. Added to this, explicitly incorporating all chemical and structural features, that might influence a specific crystal property into the GNN encoder, is a challenging task. In this work, we propose a soft prompt learning framework that captures latent features essential for property prediction, which are not explicitly provided to the GNN. We introduce a novel multilevel graph prompt learning framework comprising both node-level and graph-level soft prompts. At the node level, we capture the local chemical semantics of different atom types, while at the graph level, we encode the global structural symmetry of the crystal graph. Our proposed prompt learning framework is lightweight and seamlessly integrates with any existing GNN encoder. Extensive experiments on popular benchmark datasets show that incorporating prompt learning significantly improves (3\% - 15\%) the performance of state-of-the-art GNN models in crystal property prediction tasks. Furthermore, the learned soft prompts enable cross-property knowledge transfer, enhancing prediction performance for properties with limited training data. Code is available at https://github.com/shrimonmuke0202/Prompt.git

AI.tldr: Proposes a multilevel soft prompt learning framework for crystal property prediction that augments GNNs with node-level and graph-level prompts, yielding 3-15% gains and enabling cross-property transfer.
AI.motivation: Domain-specific graph encodings for crystal properties inflate model size and rely on expert-crafted features; it is difficult to encode all relevant chemical/structural factors explicitly, motivating latent feature learning.
AI.method: Introduce a lightweight soft prompt learning framework that can be integrated with any GNN encoder. It uses node-level prompts to capture local chemical semantics of atom types and graph-level prompts to encode global structural symmetry of the crystal graph.
AI.result: Empirical results on benchmark datasets show 3%–15% performance improvements over state-of-the-art GNNs. Learned prompts enable cross-property knowledge transfer, benefiting properties with limited training data.
AI.conclusion: Soft prompt learning provides a plug‑and‑play augmentation for crystal-property GNNs, capturing latent features not provided to the model and enabling transfer across properties.

title: Super-Generalist: Towards Comprehensive and Accurate Medical Image Understanding via Generalist-Specialist Synergy
summary: Medical images require comprehensive and accurate interpretation to support the diagnosis of diverse clincial conditions. Recent vision-language generalist models offer broad task coverage and promising zero-shot capabilities, yet often lack fine-grained anatomical and lesion awareness for reliable diagnosis and spatial interpretability. In contrast, supervised specialist models achieve strong performance on specific tasks but typically lack generalization across diseases and anatomies. In this work, we present SuG, a Super-Generalist framework that unifies generalist vision-language learning with specialist objectives, enabling both broad generalization and specialist-level diagnostic capability. We perform specialist-enhanced vision-language alignment in SuG by incorporating spatial priors from multiple segmentation experts, including anatomy, class-specific lesion and class-agnostic lesion segmentors that captures lesions beyond anatomies annotated during training. To improve lesion grounding capability, we leverage lesion masks as spatial priors to calibrate text-conditioned visual attention, encouraging disease-related semantics to focus on clinically relevant regions. We evaluate SuG on extensive chest and abdominal CT benchmarks, including CT-RATE, Merlin, MedVL-CT69K, and several in-house tumor datasets. SuG achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of disease diagnosis tasks and surpasses specialist models on several critical tumor diagnosis benchmarks. Furthermore, SuG demonstrates strong lesion grounding capability, including robust generalization to lesion types lacking class-specific supervision.

AI.tldr: A unified SuG framework that blends vision-language generalist learning with specialist segmentation-guided objectives to enable broad generalization and accurate, spatially grounded diagnosis in medical CT, achieving state-of-the-art results and robust lesion grounding, even for unseen lesion types.
AI.motivation: Bridge the gap between generalist vision-language models (broad task coverage, zero-shot potential) and supervised specialist models (high task accuracy but limited generalization) by introducing spatial priors from segmentation experts to improve anatomical and lesion awareness and interpretability in medical imaging.
AI.method: Train a Super-Generalist (SuG) by specialist-enhanced vision-language alignment: incorporate spatial priors from anatomy, class-specific lesion, and class-agnostic lesion segmentors into the vision-language alignment; use lesion masks to calibrate text-conditioned visual attention; evaluate on chest and abdominal CT benchmarks (CT-RATE, Merlin, MedVL-CT69K) and in-house tumor datasets.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of disease diagnosis tasks; surpasses some specialist models on key tumor benchmarks; demonstrates strong lesion grounding and generalization to lesion types lacking class-specific supervision.
AI.conclusion: SuG provides a practical framework that achieves both broad generalization and precise lesion-aware diagnosis with improved spatial interpretability in medical imaging, validated on diverse CT benchmarks.

title: Correlation-Aware Contextual Bandits with Surrogate Rewards for LLM Routing
summary: We study contextual bandit problems with correlated arms and access to surrogate reward signals produced by a machine learning model, motivated by applications such as large language model (LLM) routing. Unlike classical contextual bandits that rely solely on bandit feedback and assume conditional independence across arms, our setting allows context-dependent inter-arm correlations and auxiliary reward information that may be noisy or misspecified. We propose algorithms that leverage such surrogate rewards through two complementary designs. A coupled reward-mixing approach pools true and surrogate rewards to accelerate learning when surrogate signals are reliable, while a decoupled prediction-mixing approach maintains separate estimators for bandit feedback and surrogate rewards and adaptively combines their predictions. This decoupling yields robustness to surrogate misspecification, recovering regret guarantees comparable to reward-only bandit methods in the worst case, while achieving improved regret when surrogate predictions are sufficiently informative. We provide theoretical regret analyses for both approaches and evaluate them on LLM routing benchmarks under varying accuracy versus cost trade-offs. The results demonstrate improved sample efficiency and consistently better accuracy-cost trade-offs compared to standard contextual bandit baselines and strong static routing methods.

AI.tldr: Proposes two designs (coupled reward-mixing and decoupled prediction-mixing) for contextual bandits with correlated arms and surrogate rewards; analyzes regret and demonstrates improved sample efficiency and accuracy-cost trade-offs, especially when surrogates are informative.
AI.motivation: To handle context-dependent inter-arm correlations and noisy/misspecified surrogate signals in contextual bandits, motivated by applications like LLM routing.
AI.method: 1) Coupled reward-mixing: jointly pools true and surrogate rewards to speed learning when surrogates are reliable. 2) Decoupled prediction-mixing: separate estimators for bandit feedback and surrogate rewards, with adaptive combining of predictions. Theoretical regret analyses are provided; experiments on LLM routing benchmarks.
AI.result: Regret guarantees in both designs; robustness to surrogate misspecification; improved regret when surrogates are informative; empirical results show better sample efficiency and accuracy-cost trade-offs versus standard contextual bandits and static routers.
AI.conclusion: Surrogate-assisted contextual bandits can achieve robust performance and enhanced efficiency; decoupled approach offers robustness and gains when surrogates are reliable, validated on LLM routing benchmarks.

title: Weaving Light and Time: Unified Harmonic-Geometric Representation Learning for Dense RGB-Event Parsing
summary: Fusing standard RGB frames with asynchronous event streams has emerged as a definitive paradigm for robust perception in degraded environments. Although unified backbones have recently gained traction in multi-modal vision, adapting them to the RGB-Event domain remains fundamentally challenging. Existing architectures either resort to decoupled dual encoders that double computational overhead, or adopt generic unified designs that fail to resolve implicit geometric parallax and cross-spectral aliasing under the extreme representational divide between dense intensity grids and sparse kinematic spikes. To transcend these bottlenecks, we present Evita, the first unified backbone specifically engineered for dedicated dense RGB-Event parsing. To achieve profound modal synergy, Evita explicitly embeds a suite of intrinsic co-learning modules directly into every encoder layer. Specifically, it features Geometric Parallax Rectification for adaptive spatial alignment, Harmonic Spectral Resonance for texture transfer exclusively in the complex frequency domain, and Transient Global Routing for event-driven asymmetric attention. To guarantee robust feature extraction against spatial misalignments and decouple representations from specific event encodings, we construct N-ImageNetV2 alongside a stochastic event representation mixing pretraining protocol, empowering the network to seamlessly accommodate arbitrary event formats in downstream tasks. Extensive evaluations across the DELIVER, DDD17, and DSEC benchmarks confirm that Evita establishes new state-of-the-art metrics while delivering a superior accuracy-latency trade-off for real-time multimodal perception.The code are publicly available at: https://github.com/chaineypung/Evita.

AI.tldr: Evita is a unified RGB–Event backbone that outperforms prior decoupled or generic fusion methods by integrating intrinsic co-learning modules (Geometric Parallax Rectification, Harmonic Spectral Resonance, Transient Global Routing) into every encoder layer and by training with a diverse, stochastic event representation protocol (N-ImageNetV2).
AI.motivation: To overcome the inefficiencies and limitations of separate dual-encoder designs and generic unified architectures that struggle with geometric parallax, cross-spectral aliasing, and cross-format event representations when fusing dense RGB frames with sparse event streams.
AI.method: Introduce Evita, a unified backbone with per-layer co-learning modules: Geometric Parallax Rectification for adaptive spatial alignment; Harmonic Spectral Resonance for texture transfer in the complex frequency domain; Transient Global Routing for event-driven asymmetric attention. Propose N-ImageNetV2 and a stochastic event representation mixing pretraining protocol to decouple representations from event encodings and enable arbitrary event formats. Evaluate on DELIVER, DDD17, and DSEC.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art metrics and favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs for real-time multimodal perception across multiple RGB-Event benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: A dedicated unified RGB–Event backbone with embedded co-learning modules and diverse pretraining enables robust, efficient fusion of dense RGB and sparse event data, addressing geometric misalignment and spectral/format heterogeneity and enabling real-time performance.

title: Variable-Length Generative Protein Design via Generalized Poisson Flow
summary: The ability to generate variable-length proteins is crucial in protein design, where the optimal length is often unknown and tightly coupled to designability. Current diffusion- and flow-based generative models typically require the protein length to be specified before sampling, limiting their flexibility in exploring the feasible design space. To address this limitation, we introduce Generalized Poisson Flow (GPFlow), a variable-length generative framework that learns the rate function of an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson process by minimizing its negative log-likelihood. We establish population-level guarantees for recovering the joint multimodal distribution and derive an upper bound on the KL divergence between the data and generated distributions. We comprehensively evaluate GPFlow across structure and sequence design, motif scaffolding, and peptide co-design, spanning Euclidean, categorical, and Riemannian modalities to fully validate its variable-length generation quality. In unconditional design, GPFlow improves structural designability and achieves the best distributional fitness for sequence design compared to their corresponding fixed-length baselines, while perfectly recovering the length distribution. In conditional motif scaffolding, GPFlow ranks first on 10 of 16 structure-based design tasks with significantly more unique successes and also achieves more passed tasks in sequence-based design. In peptide co-design, GPFlow remains competitive even without access to a native-length oracle.

AI.tldr: GPFlow enables variable-length protein generation by learning the rate function of an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson process, with theoretical guarantees and strong empirical performance across structure/sequence design, motif scaffolding, and peptide co-design.
AI.motivation: Current diffusion- and flow-based protein generators require a fixed length, limiting exploration of design space where optimal length is unknown and linked to designability. A flexible, variable-length generative framework is needed to expand feasible designs.
AI.method: Introduce Generalized Poisson Flow (GPFlow), which learns the rate function of an inhomogeneous generalized Poisson process by minimizing its negative log-likelihood. The approach provides population-level guarantees for recovering the joint multimodal distribution and a bound on the KL divergence between data and generated distributions. Evaluation spans structure and sequence design, motif scaffolding, and peptide co-design across Euclidean, categorical, and Riemannian modalities.
AI.result: GPFlow improves unconditional design by increasing structural designability and achieving the best distributional fitness for sequence design relative to fixed-length baselines, while perfectly recovering the length distribution. In conditional motif scaffolding, it ranks first on 10 of 16 structure-based tasks and yields more unique successes and passed sequence-design tasks. In peptide co-design, GPFlow remains competitive even without access to a native-length oracle.
AI.conclusion: GPFlow demonstrates effective, flexible variable-length protein generation with theoretical guarantees and strong empirical performance across multiple design settings and modalities, enabling exploration of design spaces without prespecifying length.

title: What Pixels Are Enough? SEAMS: Sufficiency Saliency via MSE-Preservation Soft-Masks
summary: Saliency maps are most useful when they identify the image regions that are sufficient to preserve a model's behaviour. We introduce SEAMS, a sufficiency-based saliency method that directly optimises a soft mask using a preservation objective. Given a frozen differentiable model output, such as a class probability, CLS embedding, or token representation, SEAMS searches for a compact mask that preserves the selected output. The approach relies on a simple optimisation framework based on soft masks, a learnable budget, and a three-way image composite generated entirely from the query image. As a result, it requires no auxiliary distractor dataset, architecture-specific attribution mechanism, or differentiable top-k relaxation. Experiments with frozen ViT-S/16 and ConvNeXt models show that the same optimisation pipeline can generate object-level, class-conditioned, and token-level explanations by changing only the preserved target. The resulting masks are compact, interpretable, stable across random initialisations, and competitive on insertion and deletion benchmarks. Our results also indicate that different architectures often rely on different sufficient evidence while achieving similar preservation fidelity, highlighting the architecture-dependent nature of visual explanations.

AI.tldr: SEAMS is a sufficiency-based saliency method that directly optimizes a soft mask to preserve a frozen model's output using a learnable budget and a three-way image composite; it yields compact, architecture-dependent explanations across object-level, class-conditioned, and token-level tasks and is competitive on insertion/deletion benchmarks without using auxiliary data.
AI.motivation: Current saliency methods often rely on heuristics or gradient-based attributions that may not reflect the minimal region sufficient to preserve a model's behavior. SEAMS seeks a principled, data-free optimization of a mask that preserves a chosen output, highlighting truly sufficient regions and demonstrating architecture-dependent evidence for explanations.
AI.method: Optimize a soft mask directly with a preservation objective on a frozen differentiable model output (e.g., class probability, CLS embedding, or token representation). Use a learnable budget and a three-way image composite constructed from the query image. No auxiliary distractor data, architecture-specific attribution mechanism, or differentiable top-k relaxation is required. Demonstrated on frozen ViT-S/16 and ConvNeXt, enabling object-level, class-conditioned, and token-level explanations by varying the preserved target.
AI.result: The resulting masks are compact, interpretable, and stable across random initializations. They perform competitively on insertion and deletion benchmarks. The same optimization pipeline can produce object-level, class-conditioned, and token-level explanations by altering the preserved target, highlighting the architecture-dependent nature of explanations.
AI.conclusion: SEAMS demonstrates that sufficiency-based saliency is feasible without auxiliary data or specialized attribution tricks. The approach reveals that different architectures rely on different sufficient cues to preserve the same output, underscoring architecture dependence in visual explanations and offering a flexible, robust saliency framework.

title: Learning More from Less: Reinforcement Learning from Hindsight
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to post-train vision-language-action (VLA) models, but every update consumes robot rollouts that are slow and costly to collect, making sample efficiency a central concern. Manipulation tasks typically provide only sparse rewards, so a weak policy fails almost every rollout early in training and has little to learn from, even when those failures execute coherent behavior. Such a failure, however, is a success at a different task. We present Learning from Hindsight (LfH), which brings hindsight relabeling to RL post-training of VLAs by scoring failed rollouts against the tasks they actually achieved. A single vision-language model relabels both the instruction and the reward, proposing a hindsight instruction for a group of failed rollouts and scoring how well each satisfies it, and the policy trains on the relabeled and original rollouts jointly. Because VLAs generalize across language, relabeling in language lets the policy learn more from the same trajectories. On out-of-distribution LIBERO-PRO tasks, where standard RL improves only slowly, LfH achieves $5\times$ improvement in sample efficiency, and outperforms a dense progress-reward baseline. The gains hold across VLA backbones and on a physical Franka robot.

AI.tldr: LfH applies hindsight relabeling to post-training RL for vision-language-action models, relabeling failures with hindsight instructions and rewards to improve sample efficiency; achieves 5x gains on LIBERO-PRO and works on real robot.
AI.motivation: Sample inefficiency in RL with sparse rewards for VLAs; many failure rollouts contain information relevant to other tasks if relabeled with appropriate instructions; language generalization enables reuse across tasks.
AI.method: A single VLA model generates hindsight instructions for a batch of failed rollouts and scores them; relabels both instruction and reward; policy trains on relabeled and original rollouts jointly; supports multiple VLA backbones; evaluated on LIBERO-PRO and a Franka robot.
AI.result: 5x improvement in sample efficiency on LIBERO-PRO tasks; outperforms a dense progress-reward baseline; gains robust across backbones and on real hardware.
AI.conclusion: LfH demonstrates effective cross-task learning via language-based hindsight relabeling, improving data efficiency and generalization for post-training VLAs in manipulation.

title: TSR-Ego: Temporally Guided Stereo Refinement Framework for Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
summary: Egocentric 3D human pose estimation from head-mounted stereo cameras is challenging due to fisheye distortion, severe self-occlusion, and frequent truncation of body joints outside the camera field of view. Recent stereo egocentric methods have improved performance through heatmap lifting, stereo correspondence, and transformer-based refinement, but they often rely heavily on frame-local evidence or use temporal information only as auxiliary pose-level context. This limits robustness when current-frame stereo cues are weak, occluded, or ambiguous. We propose TSR-Ego, a temporally guided stereo framework that couples short-term motion evidence with projection-guided feature sampling. The model first enriches dense stereo feature maps using a causal depthwise-separable temporal convolution, allowing past visual evidence to influence the feature space before deformable cross-attention. A single-stage causal stereo decoder then refines learned 3D joint queries through temporal self-attention, joint self-attention, and fisheye deformable stereo cross-attention, using the evolving pose estimate to generate 2D sampling references. Unlike methods that apply temporal reasoning mainly after pose prediction, TSR-Ego uses motion context to shape both the sampled stereo features and the joint representations while preserving online inference without future frames. Experiments on UnrealEgo2 and UnrealEgo-RW show state-of-the-art performance, with especially strong gains on real-world sequences.

AI.tldr: TSR-Ego is a temporally guided stereo framework for online egocentric 3D pose estimation that uses causal temporal features and a single-stage causal stereo decoder with deformable cross-attention, achieving state-of-the-art results on UnrealEgo2 and UnrealEgo-RW.
AI.motivation: Existing stereo egocentric methods heavily rely on frame-local cues or post-hoc temporal reasoning, which degrades robustness when current-frame stereo cues are weak, occluded, or truncated. There is a need for online, motion-informed feature sampling and pose refinement that can leverage short-term motion without future frames.
AI.method: Enriches dense stereo features with a causal depthwise-separable temporal convolution, enabling past evidence to influence the feature space before deformable cross-attention. A single-stage causal stereo decoder refines 3D joint queries through temporal self-attention, joint self-attention, and fisheye deformable stereo cross-attention, using the evolving pose estimate to generate 2D sampling references, while preserving online inference (no future frames).
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on UnrealEgo2 and UnrealEgo-RW, with especially strong gains on real-world sequences.
AI.conclusion: Motion-guided sampling and pose-driven, online stereo refinement effectively improve robustness to occlusions and truncations in egocentric 3D pose estimation, validating the approach and its applicability to real-world data.

title: COBS: Cumulant Order Block Sparse Attention
summary: Block sparse attention is a hardware friendly way to alleviate the key-value (KV) cache read bottleneck in large language models (LLMs). However, it is not prevalent among leading open-weight LLMs, which rely instead on dense attention or fine-grained selection, thereby motivating our analysis. We study DeepSeek's Native Sparse Attention (NSA) as a representative method, whose three-branch design lets us isolate block selection, the most challenging and consequential stage. We formalize selection and reduce it to ranking blocks by a single quantity, the attention mass: the sum of a block's attention scores. We show that if selection retrieves the blocks with the largest attention mass, block sparse attention can match the quality of dense attention. However, computing the exact attention mass requires reading every key, so the problem of block selection ultimately reduces to approximating this mass from a compact summary instead of the full keys. Via a cumulant expansion, we show why existing methods falter: their selection strategies attempt to estimate the attention mass, but are confined to a first-order approximation. Therefore, we propose COBS (Cumulant Order Block Sparse Attention), an attention method that builds on NSA, incorporating a novel selector that stores a compressed second-order statistic per block. On the 32k RULER long-context retrieval benchmark, COBS raises the NSA baseline's mean score from 0.2999 to 0.8195, approaching dense attention at 0.9040 and closing about 86% of the gap, while using only 1.21x the KV cache read traffic of the NSA baseline and 15.15x less read traffic than dense. The same model preserves short-context behavior and attains lower position-wise negative log-likelihood (NLL) than dense attention in our comparison.

AI.tldr: COBS uses a cumulant-based second-order block selector to improve block-sparse attention (NSA), achieving near-dense performance with modest KV-cache traffic on long-context tasks.
AI.motivation: Alleviate the KV cache bottleneck in LLMs and close the gap between block-sparse and dense attention by improving the block-selection phase; formalize the selection problem and identify limitations of first-order approximations.
AI.method: Formalize selection as ranking blocks by attention mass; show exact mass is costly to compute; use cumulant expansion to explain failures of first-order methods; introduce COBS with a compressed second-order statistic per block; integrate with NSA's three-branch design; evaluate on long-context retrieval benchmarks.
AI.result: On 32k context RULER benchmark, COBS raises NSA mean score from 0.2999 to 0.8195, approaching dense attention at 0.9040 and covering ~86% of the gap; KV-cache read traffic is 1.21x NSA, and ~15.15x less than dense; preserves short-context behavior and reports lower position-wise NLL than dense in comparison.
AI.conclusion: Second-order (cumulant-based) block selection enables block-sparse attention to closely match dense performance with substantially less KV-cache traffic, illustrating the practicality of NSA+COBS for long-context LLMs.

title: EvoLP: Self-Evolving Latency Predictor for Model Compression in Real-Time Edge Systems
comment: Author's accepted version. Published in IEEE Embedded Systems Letters
summary: Edge devices are increasingly utilized for deploying deep learning applications on embedded systems. The real-time nature of many applications and the limited resources of edge devices necessitate latency-targeted neural network compression. However, measuring latency on real devices is challenging and expensive. Therefore, this letter presents a novel and efficient framework, named EvoLP, to accurately predict the inference latency of models on edge devices. This predictor can evolve to achieve higher latency prediction precision during the network compression process. Experimental results demonstrate that EvoLP outperforms previous state-of-the-art approaches by being evaluated on three edge devices and four model variants. Moreover, when incorporated into a model compression framework, it effectively guides the compression process for higher model accuracy while satisfying strict latency constraints. We open source EvoLP at https://github.com/ntuliuteam/EvoLP.

AI.tldr: EvoLP is an evolutionary latency predictor for edge-device model compression that predicts inference latency to guide compression, outperforming prior methods on multiple devices and variants, and is open-sourced.
AI.motivation: Accurate latency measurement on real edge devices is costly and impractical; a fast, reliable latency predictor enables latency-targeted compression without hardware reliance, accelerating deployment of DL on embedded systems.
AI.method: Propose EvoLP, a predictive framework that evolves to improve latency prediction accuracy during the network compression process. It is evaluated across three edge devices and four model variants and integrated into a compression framework to balance accuracy and strict latency constraints.
AI.result: EvoLP achieves higher latency prediction precision than prior approaches, generalizes across multiple devices and model variants, and effectively guides compression to meet latency requirements while improving model accuracy. Open-sourcing at the provided URL.
AI.conclusion: A latency-aware, evolvable predictor like EvoLP can significantly streamline latency-constrained model compression for edge deployments and facilitate more reliable real-time DNN applications.

title: HiHR: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
comment: Accepted by ECCV2026. More modifications may be performed
summary: Aerial-Ground Person Re-IDentification (AG-ReID) aims to retrieve the same person across heterogeneous aerial and ground camera platforms. Although great progress has been made, existing methods remain suboptimal due to the direct feature alignment across views, overlooking view-specific cues. To address this issue, we propose a novel Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation (HiHR) framework for AG-ReID. More specifically, we first extract multi-granularity features based on pre-trained visual-text encoders. Then, we propose a Text-guided Multi-granularity Fusion (TMF) to fuse multi-granularity features and enhance the representation ability of identity features. Furthermore, we introduce the Hierarchical Hyperbolic Learning (HHL) to construct a hierarchical feature structure in a hyperbolic space. This hierarchy includes a coarse level that ensures identity separability and cross-view consistency, and a fine level that preserves view-specific discriminative cues. As a result, our proposed framework can effectively aggregate view-invariant and view-specific discriminative features for AG-ReID. Extensive experiments on four AG-ReID benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. The source code is available at https://github.com/YangQiWei3/HiHR.

AI.tldr: A novel Hierarchical Hyperbolic Representation (HiHR) framework for aerial-ground person re-ID that uses text-guided multi-granularity feature fusion and hyperbolic hierarchy to capture both view-invariant and view-specific cues, achieving strong results on four AG-ReID benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Cross-view misalignment and neglect of view-specific cues hinder AG-ReID; there is a need to jointly model identity-consistent and view-specific discriminative information, leveraging hierarchical representations in hyperbolic space.
AI.method: 1) Extract multi-granularity features via pre-trained visual-text encoders. 2) Use Text-guided Multi-granularity Fusion (TMF) to fuse features and enhance identity representation. 3) Introduce Hierarchical Hyperbolic Learning (HHL) to build a coarse-to-fine hierarchical feature structure in hyperbolic space, with a coarse level for identity separability and cross-view consistency and a fine level for view-specific discriminative cues.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on four AG-ReID benchmarks demonstrate the framework's effectiveness; source code is provided at the given repository URL.
AI.conclusion: HiHR effectively aggregates both view-invariant and view-specific discriminative features for AG-ReID, leveraging a hierarchical hyperbolic representation and text-guided feature fusion to improve cross-view matching.

title: Pitfalls and Remedies for Multi-Task Bayesian Optimization
summary: Bayesian optimization routinely warm-starts a target experiment with data from related source tasks, and the multi-task Gaussian process is the textbook surrogate for the job. We revisit this default in a controlled setting and find that it misestimates the cross-task correlation even in the simplest non-trivial case, affinely related source and target tasks, where a working transfer learning method should obviously succeed. We trace the failure to two independent structural mechanisms. Per-task standardization, the textbook fix for the affine slice ambiguity, propagates a finite-sample alignment error into the recovered correlation. The marginal likelihood itself identifies the correlation only at a per-sample rate that a Gaussian process at non-overlapping designs further dilutes. We propose three conservative remedies that follow from the analysis: promoting per-task means and scales to model parameters, restricting the task covariance to non-negative correlations, and co-locating part of the source and target designs. Across synthetic multi-task problems and surrogate-based hyperparameter tuning transfer, these remedies recover the target-only baseline on the simple instances, while the broader failure persists on harder instances and across most rank-based and latent-context variants.

AI.tldr: Re-evaluates multi-task GP warm-starts in Bayesian optimization, showing that affine-related source/target tasks misestimate cross-task correlation due to per-task standardization and per-sample likelihood; proposes three remedies (per-task means/scales as parameters, non-negative correlations, co-locating designs). Remedial fixes help simple cases but fail for harder, rank-based/latent-context variants.
AI.motivation: Warm-starting Bayesian optimization with data from related tasks is standard, but the canonical multi-task GP surrogate may misestimate cross-task correlations, hampering transfer efficiency. The study isolates two structural causes and tests remedies.
AI.method: The authors perform a controlled analysis of cross-task correlation estimation in multi-task Gaussian processes under affine relationships between source and target tasks. They identify two structural mechanisms: per-task standardization propagating finite-sample alignment error into correlation estimates, and per-sample rate-limited correlation identification by the marginal likelihood, especially with non-overlapping designs. They propose three remedies and evaluate on synthetic multi-task problems and surrogate-based hyperparameter tuning transfer, comparing against a target-only baseline.
AI.result: Three conservative remedies: (1) model per-task means and scales as parameters (avoiding fixed standardization), (2) restrict task covariance to non-negative correlations, (3) co-locate part of source and target designs. In experiments, these remedies recover the target-only baseline on simple affine instances; however, the broader failure persists on harder instances and across most rank-based and latent-context variants.
AI.conclusion: Cross-task transfer via multi-task GP for Bayesian optimization is fragile: even affine relatedness can be misestimated due to standardization and sampling effects. Targeted fixes can restore performance in simple cases, but the failures persist in more complex transfer settings, indicating limits of current MTGP payoffs and suggesting careful model/design choices to mitigate misestimation.

title: YeTI: You Only Need Two Noisy Images for Real-World sRGB Noise Generation
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Includes supplementary material
summary: Real-world sRGB image denoising remains challenging due to the nonlinear characteristics of sensor noise and the difficulty of acquiring aligned clean-noisy image pairs. Supervised denoisers often overfit to limited paired datasets, while self-supervised methods still depend on sufficiently diverse noisy observations. These limitations motivate scalable noise synthesis methods that can model real-world noise without clean ground truth or camera metadata. We propose YeTI, a real-world sRGB noise generation framework that learns from only two noisy observations of the same scene. YeTI uses a Reconstruction Autoencoder to disentangle scene structure and noise characteristics, and models the latent noise distribution with a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer trained using consistency objectives. Given a single noisy input at inference time, YeTI generates realistic, signal-dependent noise while preserving the underlying scene content. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of YeTI across real-world benchmarks. We evaluate noise generation on SIDD and further assess generalization on SIDD+, MAI2021, and SID, covering smartphone and diverse consumer-camera sensors. Downstream denoising results on DND further show that denoisers trained with YeTI-synthesized images achieve strong real-world performance, highlighting the practical value of clean-image-free and metadata-free noise generation.

AI.tldr: YeTI is a real-world sRGB noise generation framework that learns from only two noisy observations of the same scene to synthesize realistic, signal-dependent noise via a Reconstruction Autoencoder and a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer, enabling clean-image-free noise generation for training denoisers across real-world benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Real-world sRGB denoising is hindered by nonlinear sensor noise and lack of aligned clean-noisy pairs. Conventional supervised methods overfit on small paired datasets; self-supervised methods require diverse noisy observations. A scalable, metadata-free noise generator is needed.
AI.method: A Reconstruction Autoencoder separates scene structure from noise; a one-step Conditional Diffusion Transformer models the latent noise distribution, trained with consistency objectives. Inference uses a single noisy input to produce noise consistent with the scene, preserving content. Training uses only two noisy observations of the same scene; no clean ground truth or camera metadata needed.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world benchmarks show YeTI's noise generation is realistic and improves downstream denoising. Evaluation on SIDD, SIDD+, MAI2021, SID demonstrates generalization across smartphone and consumer cameras. Denoisers trained with YeTI-synthesized data achieve strong real-world performance on DND.
AI.conclusion: YeTI enables clean-image-free, metadata-free synthesis of realistic noise from minimal data, offering practical value for training robust denoisers in real-world settings.

title: A Survey on the Green Development of Large Models: From Resource-Efficient Architectures to Hardware-Software Co-Design
comment: This paper has been accepted by CJE (2026), paper homepage: https://cje.ejournal.org.cn/article/doi/10.23919/cje.2025.00.438
summary: The rapid expansion of large-scale AI models has led to significant performance breakthroughs across diverse domains, yet it has also raised critical concerns regarding computational costs, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the green development of large models, emphasizing resource-efficient architectures and full-stack hardware-software co-design. We systematically review recent advances in efficient model construction, including attention operator optimization, linear-complexity architectures, and model sparsification and merging, as well as training and deployment strategies such as data-efficient learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and computational compression. Beyond algorithmic improvements, we explore energy-efficient AI hardware, including mainstream AI chips, memory optimization, cross-platform deployment, and sustainable infrastructure. Furthermore, we examine how large models are being applied to sustainability-critical domains such as DeepSeek, remote sensing interpretation, national-scale infrastructure, and global initiatives. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, highlighting the need for continual learning paradigms, memory-centric hardware, and standardized evaluation protocols. This survey aims to offer a holistic roadmap toward sustainable, scalable, and socially responsible development of large models. Paper homepage: https://cje.ejournal.org.cn/article/doi/10.23919/cje.2025.00.438

AI.tldr: A comprehensive survey of sustainable development for large AI models, covering efficient architectures, training/inference methods, hardware, deployment, and governance, with a roadmap for future work.
AI.motivation: Rising costs and environmental impact of scaling AI demand practical solutions for energy efficiency and responsible deployment.
AI.method: Systematic literature review across model efficiency techniques (attention optimization, linear-time architectures, sparsification/merging), training/deployment strategies (data-efficient learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, compression), energy-efficient hardware (chips, memory optimization, cross-platform deployment), sustainability-focused applications, and forward-looking challenges.
AI.result: Produces a holistic taxonomy and roadmap, highlighting design principles, trade-offs, and actionable guidance for researchers and practitioners.
